"representation learning"

1. how should we use fancy machine learning models -- one idea, broadly construed, is to take various "non-euclidean" kinds of data (read: anything that isn't a number in a csv), embed it using some foundation model or something along those lines. lots of people are doing this; doing it well is clearly important and smart

2. in this literature, the framing is always that we are learning a representation of confounders; that is, things that we need to adjust for to get valid causal estimates. but what should we actually adjust for @cinelli2022:

- TODO

what should not adjust for:

- mediators
- colliders
- post-outcome variables
- post-treatment variables

```{r}
#| label: fig-bad-controls
#| fig-cap: "Four kinds of bad controls. Red nodes are the variable you should not adjust for; grey nodes are unmeasured."
#| fig-alt: "Four small directed acyclic graphs arranged in a 2x2 grid, each with treatment X and outcome Y as dark grey nodes and a bad control highlighted in red. Top left: a mediator M sits on the path from X to M to Y, in addition to a direct X to Y edge; adjusting for M blocks part of the X to Y effect. Top right: a collider C is a common effect of X and Y; adjusting for C opens a spurious path between X and Y. Bottom left: an unmeasured node U causes both an outcome Y and a post-treatment variable Z, which is also caused by X; adjusting for Z amplifies bias from the unmeasured confounder U. Bottom right: a post-outcome variable P is caused by Y, which is caused by X; adjusting for P conditions on something that occurs after Y."
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| column: body-outset
#| code-fold: true
library(ggdag)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)

node_colors <- c(
  exposure = "grey30",
  outcome  = "grey30",
  bad      = "#B2182B",
  latent   = "grey70"
)

plot_bad_control <- function(dag_data, title, subtitle) {
  ggplot(dag_data, aes(x = x, y = y, xend = xend, yend = yend)) +
    geom_dag_edges(edge_color = "grey50") +
    geom_dag_point(aes(color = role), size = 16) +
    geom_dag_text(color = "white", size = 3.5, fontface = "bold") +
    scale_color_manual(values = node_colors, guide = "none") +
    labs(title = title, subtitle = subtitle) +
    theme_dag() +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9, hjust = 0.5, color = "grey30")
    )
}

# mediator: X -> M -> Y, X -> Y
mediator <- dagify(
  Y ~ X + M,
  M ~ X,
  exposure = "X",
  outcome = "Y",
  coords = list(x = c(X = 0, M = 1, Y = 2), y = c(X = 0, M = 1, Y = 0))
) |>
  tidy_dagitty()
mediator$data$role <- ifelse(mediator$data$name == "M", "bad", "outcome")

# collider: X -> C <- Y, X -> Y
collider <- dagify(
  Y ~ X,
  C ~ X + Y,
  exposure = "X",
  outcome = "Y",
  coords = list(x = c(X = 0, C = 1, Y = 2), y = c(X = 0, C = 1, Y = 0))
) |>
  tidy_dagitty()
collider$data$role <- ifelse(collider$data$name == "C", "bad", "outcome")

# post-treatment variable: X -> Z <- U -> Y, X -> Y, U unmeasured
post_treatment <- dagify(
  Y ~ X + U,
  Z ~ X + U,
  exposure = "X",
  outcome = "Y",
  latent = "U",
  coords = list(x = c(X = 0, Z = 1, U = 1, Y = 2), y = c(X = 0, Z = 1, U = 2, Y = 0))
) |>
  tidy_dagitty()
post_treatment$data$role <- dplyr::case_when(
  post_treatment$data$name == "Z" ~ "bad",
  post_treatment$data$name == "U" ~ "latent",
  TRUE ~ "outcome"
)

# post-outcome variable: X -> Y -> P
post_outcome <- dagify(
  Y ~ X,
  P ~ Y,
  exposure = "X",
  outcome = "Y",
  coords = list(x = c(X = 0, Y = 1, P = 2), y = c(X = 0, Y = 0, P = 0))
) |>
  tidy_dagitty()
post_outcome$data$role <- ifelse(post_outcome$data$name == "P", "bad", "outcome")

p1 <- plot_bad_control(mediator$data, "mediator", "blocks part of the X → Y effect")
p2 <- plot_bad_control(collider$data, "collider", "opens a spurious path between X and Y")
p3 <- plot_bad_control(post_treatment$data, "post-treatment variable", "amplifies bias from unmeasured U")
p4 <- plot_bad_control(post_outcome$data, "post-outcome variable", "hasn't happened yet when X acts")

(p1 | p2) / (p3 | p4)
```

3. okay, so we have some image/network/text, we estimate some embeddings, and then we go forth and adjust for it. when can this go wrong: whenever the latent features in the embeddings are mediators, colliders, etc, etc

4. how can you know if the latent features you learned in the embedding are mediators, colliders, etc. in general you can't tell just from the embedding, since it only captures statistical dependence, not causal role. you need something from outside the data, like a plausible DAG, timing info, or an intervention, to sort that out.
